title: The 10,000-Year Clock
summary: Danny Hillis's clock, built by Long Now in a Texas mountain: designed to tick for ten millennia, powered by thermal cycles, chiming uniquely each millennium.
body:

title: Checksum Demo: Fixity in Code
summary: Fixity checks are deep-time archiving's heartbeat: hash the data, rehash later, compare.
body:
Fixity checks are deep-time archiving's heartbeat: hash the data, rehash later, compare. The same SHA-256 that guards blockchains guards archives.

Context: this record is part of the Deeptime Archiving catalog — deep-time archiving preserves knowledge across millennia: the 10,000-year clock, the rosetta disk, arctic vaults, and dna storage.

program.code:
# Fixity check: the archivist's heartbeat
import hashlib
def sha256_file(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
payload = b"Knowledge for the year 12026."
h1 = sha256_file(payload)
print(f"stored:  {h1[:32]}...")
print(f"recheck: {sha256_file(payload)[:32]}...")
print("match:", h1 == sha256_file(payload))
